findings.reason: Before cancellation, the first stop consumes the one-time action and sets its result to true. The second stop skips that action and returns its initial false value.
A second stop can return false after the first stop prevented the callback from running.

findings.fragment: The stop function does not wait for f to complete before returning.
findings.reason: The contract requires callers who need to know whether the callback has completed to coordinate with it explicitly.

findings.fragment: Multiple calls to AfterFunc on a context operate independently;
findings.reason: Each call creates a separate registration, and the next line explicitly rules out replacement.

findings.fragment: If ctx is already canceled, AfterFunc calls f immediately in its own goroutine.
findings.reason: The contract explicitly provides for a separate callback goroutine when the context is already canceled at registration.
The registration stores the context passed as its parent. Reassigning only the caller's local variable leaves that stored parent intact.

findings.fragment: AfterFunc arranges to call f in its own goroutine after ctx is canceled.
findings.reason: The callback contract describes when the callback is scheduled and leaves latency thresholds and incident reporting to application policy.
findings.question: OPEN: Does the source specify any requirement for the application to report callback latency above ten milliseconds as an incident?

cases.claim: Stopping a registered callback before cancellation returns true on the first stop and false on a second stop.
A false stop result proves that the callback is currently running.
Stopping an already started callback waits until that callback finishes.
Two AfterFunc registrations on the same context operate independently rather than replacing each other.
Registration on an already canceled context still schedules the callback in its own goroutine.
After registration, reassigning only the caller local context variable redirects the registration to the new context.
The application is required to report callback latency above ten milliseconds as an incident.
